entries.sanskrit: अष्टमे समभूद् ब्रह्मा नाभेस् तु जल-शायिनः । तम् अजानञ् जले बिभ्यत् तपसापोषयद् विभुम् ॥ श्रोतारम् अभिनन्दति । सतां सेवितुं योग्यः । बत अहो । यत् यस्माद् इहास्मिन् वंशे लोक-पालो धर्म-राजस् त्वं बभूविथ जातोऽसि । कथं-भूतः ? भगवान् एव प्रधान-भूतो यस्य सः । अत्र हेतुः---अजितेति । प्रतिक्षणं नूतनयसि नवीनां करोषि ॥१॥
word_for_word: aṣṭame samabhūd brahmā nābhes tu jala-śāyinaḥ
In the eighth chapter Brahmā arose from the navel of the Lord reclining in the waters. Not knowing Him
tam ajānañ jale bibhyat tapasāpoṣayad vibhum
Brahmā was afraid in the water
śrotāram abhinandati
and the Lord nourished that powerful one through austerity. Maitreya praises Vidura as the worthy hearer and says
satāṃ sevituṃ yogyaḥ
you were born in this lineage as the guardian of the world and as one whose chief is Bhagavān
bata aho
hearing the Bhāgavata
yat yasmād ihāsmin vaṃśe loka-pālo dharma-rājas tvaṃ babhūvitha jāto’si
you have become purified and are fit to hear the account.
kathaṃ-bhūtaḥ ? bhagavān eva pradhāna-bhūto yasya saḥ
you have become purified and are fit to hear the account.
atra hetuḥ
you have become purified and are fit to hear the account.
ajiteti
you have become purified and are fit to hear the account.
pratikṣaṇaṃ nūtanayasi navīnāṃ karoṣi
you have become purified and are fit to hear the account.
entries.literal_english: In the eighth chapter Brahmā arose from the navel of the Lord reclining in the waters. Not knowing Him, Brahmā was afraid in the water, and the Lord nourished that powerful one through austerity. Maitreya praises Vidura as the worthy hearer and says: you were born in this lineage as the guardian of the world and as one whose chief is Bhagavān; hearing the Bhāgavata, you have become purified and are fit to hear the account.

entries.sanskrit: अल्प-सुखाय महद्-दुःखं प्राप्तानां तस्य दुःखस्य विरमाय प्रवर्तये प्रारभे ॥२॥
word_for_word: alpa-sukhāya mahad-duḥkhaṃ prāptānāṃ tasya
I begin this narration in order to end the great
duḥkhasya viramāya pravartaye prārabhe
suffering of those who have received only a little happiness.
entries.literal_english: I begin this narration in order to end the great suffering of those who have received only a little happiness.

entries.sanskrit: कोऽसौ भगवान् ? केभ्यश् च ऋषिभ्य आह ? कथं च त्वया प्राप्तं ? इत्य् अपेक्षायाम् आह---आसीनम् इति सप्तभिः । उर्व्यां पाताल-तले अकुण्ठ-सत्त्वम् अप्रतिहत-ज्ञानम् । अतः सङ्कर्षणात् परस्य श्री-वासुदेवस्य ॥३॥
word_for_word: ko’sau bhagavān ? kebhyaś ca ṛṣibhya āha ? kathaṃ ca tvayā prāptaṃ ? ity apekṣāyām āha
Who is this Bhagavān
āsīnam iti saptabhiḥ
from whom sages did he hear
urvyāṃ pātāla-tale akuṇṭha-sattvam apratihata-jñānam
and how did you obtain this knowledge? In answer
ataḥ saṅkarṣaṇāt parasya śrī-vāsudevasya
Maitreya begins seven verses with “seated.” He was seated on the earth
entries.literal_english: Who is this Bhagavān, from whom sages did he hear, and how did you obtain this knowledge? In answer, Maitreya begins seven verses with “seated.” He was seated on the earth, in the lower world, with unobstructed spiritual power and unobstructed knowledge; he is superior to Saṅkarṣaṇa and to Śrī Vāsudeva.

entries.sanskrit: तम् एव विशिनष्टि---स्वम् एव धिष्ण्यं स्वीयम् आश्रयं वासुदेव-संज्ञं परमानन्द-रूपं ध्यान-पथेऽनुभूय बहु मानयन्तं सर्वोत्कर्षेण पूजयन्तम् । प्रत्यग्-धृतम् अन्तर्-मुखी-कृतं नेत्राम्बुज-मुकुलं किञ्चिद् उन्मीलयन्तम् । कृपावलोकेन सनत्-कुमारादीनाम् अभ्युदयार्थम् ॥४॥
word_for_word: tam eva viśinaṣṭi
He further identifies Him
svam eva dhiṣṇyaṃ svīyam āśrayaṃ vāsudeva-saṃjñaṃ paramānanda-rūpaṃ dhyāna-pathe’nubhūya bahu mānayantaṃ sarvotkarṣeṇa pūjayantam
His own abode
pratyag-dhṛtam antar-mukhī-kṛtaṃ netrāmbuja-mukulaṃ kiñcid unmīlayantam
the support called Vāsudeva
kṛpāvalokena sanat-kumārādīnām abhyudayārtham
is the form of supreme bliss. He honors it greatly
entries.literal_english: He further identifies Him: His own abode, the support called Vāsudeva, is the form of supreme bliss. He honors it greatly, worshipping it as supreme while experiencing it on the path of meditation. His lotus eyes, drawn inward, were slightly opening; His merciful glance was for the spiritual elevation of Sanaka and the other sages.

entries.sanskrit: मुनीनां विशेषणं सार्धेन । स्वर्धुन्या उदकेनार्द्रैर् इति । श्री-भागवत-श्रवणार्थं सत्य-लोकात् पातालं प्रत्यवतरन्तो निरन्तरं गङ्गा-मध्यत एवावतीर्णा इति भावः । चरणाव् उपधीयेते । यस्मिन् पद्मे । तद् उपस्पृशन्तो नमन्तः । कथं-भूतं ? तद् आह---यत् पद्मं प्रेम-सहितं यथा भवत्य् एवं नानोपहारैः पूजयन्ति । वरार्थाः पतिकामाः ॥५॥
word_for_word: munīnāṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ sārdhena
The phrase describes the sages as moistened by the water of the celestial Gaṅgā. They descended from Satyaloka to Pātāla in order to hear the Bhāgavata
svardhunyā udakenārdrair iti
coming down through the middle of the Gaṅgā. They touched and bowed to the lotus on which His feet rested
śrī-bhāgavata-śravaṇārthaṃ satya-lokāt pātālaṃ pratyavataranto nirantaraṃ gaṅgā-madhyata evāvatīrṇā iti bhāvaḥ
and Maitreya explains the lotus as an object approached with love and reverence.
caraṇāv upadhīyete
and Maitreya explains the lotus as an object approached with love and reverence.
yasmin padme
and Maitreya explains the lotus as an object approached with love and reverence.
tad upaspṛśanto namantaḥ
and Maitreya explains the lotus as an object approached with love and reverence.
kathaṃ-bhūtaṃ ? tad āha
and Maitreya explains the lotus as an object approached with love and reverence.
yat padmaṃ prema-sahitaṃ yathā bhavaty evaṃ nānopahāraiḥ pūjayanti
and Maitreya explains the lotus as an object approached with love and reverence.
varārthāḥ patikāmāḥ
and Maitreya explains the lotus as an object approached with love and reverence.
entries.literal_english: The phrase describes the sages as moistened by the water of the celestial Gaṅgā. They descended from Satyaloka to Pātāla in order to hear the Bhāgavata, coming down through the middle of the Gaṅgā. They touched and bowed to the lotus on which His feet rested, and Maitreya explains the lotus as an object approached with love and reverence.

entries.sanskrit: कृतानि कर्माणि गृणन्तः । केन ? अनुरागेण स्खलन्ति पदानि यस्मिन्, तेन वचसा। तानि जानन्तीति तज्-ज्ञाः । सहस्रम् एव साहस्रं किरीटानां साहस्रे ये मणि-प्रवेका रत्नोत्तमाः, तैः प्रद्योतितम् उद्दाम-फणानां सहस्रं यस्य तम् अपृच्छन्न् इति पूर्वेणान्वयः ॥६॥
word_for_word: kṛtāni karmāṇi gṛṇantaḥ

They praised Him while reciting His deeds. They did so with loving speech in which their words seemed to stumble from emotion. The sages knew those deeds. The crowns of their thousands of heads shone with the finest jewels
kena ? anurāgeṇa skhalanti padāni yasmin
and they asked the Lord whose raised hoods were also adorned with thousands of radiant jewels.
tena vacasā
and they asked the Lord whose raised hoods were also adorned with thousands of radiant jewels.
tāni jānantīti taj-jñāḥ
and they asked the Lord whose raised hoods were also adorned with thousands of radiant jewels.
sahasram eva sāhasraṃ kirīṭānāṃ sāhasre ye maṇi-pravekā ratnottamāḥ
and they asked the Lord whose raised hoods were also adorned with thousands of radiant jewels.
taiḥ pradyotitam uddāma-phaṇānāṃ sahasraṃ yasya tam apṛcchann iti pūrveṇānvayaḥ
and they asked the Lord whose raised hoods were also adorned with thousands of radiant jewels.
entries.literal_english: They praised Him while reciting His deeds. They did so with loving speech in which their words seemed to stumble from emotion. The sages knew those deeds. The crowns of their thousands of heads shone with the finest jewels, and they asked the Lord whose raised hoods were also adorned with thousands of radiant jewels.

entries.sanskrit: पारमहंस्ये धर्मे मुख्यः । विवक्षमाण इत्य् आत्मनेपदं, ब्रूञ्-आदेशस्य वचेर् उभयपदित्वात् । अन्वितायानुगताय ॥८॥

vivakṣamāṇa ity ātmanepadaṃ

brūñ-ādeśasya vacer ubhayapaditvāt

anvitāyānugatāya

entries.literal_english: He is foremost in the discipline of the paramahaṃsas. “Desiring to speak” is expressed in the middle voice because the verbal root has both usages; “endowed with” means following or accompanied by.

entries.sanskrit: पुलस्त्येनोक्त इत्य् अत्रैवम् आख्यायिका । पितरं राक्षस-भक्षितं श्रुत्वा पराशरो राक्षस-सत्रे प्रवृत्तो वसिष्ठ-वचनान् निवृत्तस् ततः पुलस्त्येन स्व-सन्तति-रक्षणात् तुष्टेन वरो दत्तः पुराण-प्रवक्ता भविष्यसीति ॥९॥
word_for_word: pulastyenokta ity atraivam ākhyāyikā
The statement that it was spoken by Pulastya is explained by this account
pitaraṃ rākṣasa-bhakṣitaṃ śrutvā parāśaro rākṣasa-satre pravṛtto vasiṣṭha-vacanān nivṛttas tataḥ pulastyena sva-santati-rakṣaṇāt tuṣṭena varo dattaḥ purāṇa-pravaktā bhaviṣyasīti
after hearing that his father had been eaten by a rākṣasa
entries.literal_english: The statement that it was spoken by Pulastya is explained by this account: after hearing that his father had been eaten by a rākṣasa, Parāśara began a sacrifice for destroying the rākṣasas. He stopped at Vasiṣṭha’s words, and Pulastya, pleased that his own descendants were protected, granted him the boon that he would become a speaker of the Purāṇas.

entries.sanskrit: तद् एवं सङ्कर्षणात् संप्रदाय-प्रवृत्तिं प्रदर्श्य विभूति-कथनाय पद्मोद्भवं वक्तुम् आह---उदाप्लुतम् एकार्णवोदके निमग्नं यद् यदा आसीत् तदा अम्ईलित-दृग् अतिरोहित-चिच्-छक्तिर् एव श्री-नारायणो नेत्रे निमीलितवान् इत्य् अर्थः । माया-विनोदं परित्यज्य स्वात्म-रतौ स्वरूपानन्द एव कृतोत्सवः । अत एव निरीहो निष्क्रियः सन् ॥१०॥
word_for_word: tad evaṃ saṅkarṣaṇāt saṃpradāya-pravṛttiṃ pradarśya vibhūti-kathanāya padmodbhavaṃ vaktum āha
Having shown the continuation of the disciplic transmission from Saṅkarṣaṇa
udāplutam ekārṇavodake nimagnaṃ yad yadā āsīt tadā amīlita-dṛg atirohita-cic-chaktir eva śrī-nārāyaṇo netre nimīlitavān ity arthaḥ
Maitreya now turns to the lotus-born Brahmā in order to describe the Lord’s manifestations. When the Lord was submerged in the one ocean
māyā-vinodaṃ parityajya svātma-ratau svarūpānanda eva kṛtotsavaḥ
Nārāyaṇa closed His eyes while His consciousness remained fully present. He abandoned the sport of māyā and rested in His own self. At the appointed time
ata eva nirīho niṣkriyaḥ san
the power of time awakened Him for creation
the subtle karmic arrangement of the living beings then became visible to Him.
entries.literal_english: Having shown the continuation of the disciplic transmission from Saṅkarṣaṇa, Maitreya now turns to the lotus-born Brahmā in order to describe the Lord’s manifestations. When the Lord was submerged in the one ocean, Nārāyaṇa closed His eyes while His consciousness remained fully present. He abandoned the sport of māyā and rested in His own self. At the appointed time, the power of time awakened Him for creation; the subtle karmic arrangement of the living beings then became visible to Him.

entries.sanskrit: काल-शक्तेः प्रेरणं पुनः सृष्ट्य्-अवसरे प्रबोधनार्थम् । स्वे पदेऽधिष्ठाने। बहिर्-वृत्त्य्-अभावे दृष्टान्तः, यथानल इति ॥११॥
word_for_word: kāla-śakteḥ preraṇaṃ punaḥ sṛṣṭy-avasare prabodhanārtham
The impulse of the power of time was for
sve pade’dhiṣṭhāne
awakening Him again at the time of creation. “In
bahir-vṛtty-abhāve dṛṣṭāntaḥ
His own place” means in His own seat or abode.
yathānala iti
The absence of outward activity is illustrated by fire
that remains present though its activity is not externally manifest.
entries.literal_english: The impulse of the power of time was for awakening Him again at the time of creation. “In His own place” means in His own seat or abode. The absence of outward activity is illustrated by fire that remains present though its activity is not externally manifest.

entries.sanskrit: स्वया चिच्-छक्त्या सह वर्तमान एव योग-निद्रया स्वपन् पूर्वम् एव बोधनार्थं नियुक्तया स्व-काल-शक्त्या आसादितं प्रापितं कर्म-तन्त्रं क्रियाकलापो यस्य सः । अपीतान् लीनान् ददर्श ॥१२॥
word_for_word: svayā cic-chaktyā saha vartamāna eva yoga-nidrayā svapan pūrvam eva bodhanārthaṃ niyuktayā sva-kāla-śaktyā āsāditaṃ prāpitaṃ karma-tantraṃ kriyākalāpo yasya saḥ
While sleeping in yoga-nidrā together with His own consciousness-power
apītān līnān dadarśa
He had already been appointed to awaken by His own time-power. The network of karma had been brought to maturity
and He saw the living beings who had merged into Him.
entries.literal_english: While sleeping in yoga-nidrā together with His own consciousness-power, He had already been appointed to awaken by His own time-power. The network of karma had been brought to maturity, and He saw the living beings who had merged into Him.

entries.sanskrit: लोक-सृष्ट्य्-अर्थम् अर्थ-सूक्ष्मेऽभिनिविष्टा दृष्टिर् यस्य । कालानुसारिणा रजो-गुणेन विद्धः स-क्षोभितः सन् तनीयान् अतिसूक्ष्मोऽर्थः सूष्यन् प्रसोष्यन्न् उद्भविष्यन् नाभि-देशाद् उद्भूत इत्य् अर्थः ॥१३॥
word_for_word: loka-sṛṣṭy-artham artha-sūkṣme’bhiniviṣṭā dṛṣṭir yasya
His glance
kālānusāriṇā rajo-guṇena viddhaḥ sa-kṣobhitaḥ san tanīyān atisūkṣmo’rthaḥ sūṣyan prasoṣyann udbhaviṣyan nābhi-deśād udbhūta ity arthaḥ
intent upon the subtle cause for the creation of the worlds
was present there. Struck and agitated by rajas
entries.literal_english: His glance, intent upon the subtle cause for the creation of the worlds, was present there. Struck and agitated by rajas, in accordance with time, the subtle principle became still subtler and began to unfold; it arose from the region of His navel.

entries.sanskrit: स तनीयान् अर्थः पद्म-कोशः सन्न् उदतिष्ठत् । कर्माणि जीवादृष्टानि प्रतिप्रबोधयति यः कालस् तेन । आत्मा श्री-विष्णुर् योनिर् यस्य ॥१४॥
word_for_word: sa tanīyān arthaḥ padma-kośaḥ sann udatiṣṭhat
That subtle principle rose as the bud of a lotus. Time
karmāṇi jīvādṛṣṭāni pratiprabodhayati yaḥ kālas tena
which awakens the past actions of the living beings
ātmā śrī-viṣṇur yonir yasya
caused it to arise
Viṣṇu Himself was its source.
entries.literal_english: That subtle principle rose as the bud of a lotus. Time, which awakens the past actions of the living beings, caused it to arise; Viṣṇu Himself was its source.

entries.sanskrit: तल्-लोकात्मकं पद्मं सर्वान् गुणान् जीव-भोग्यान् अर्थान् अवभासयतीति तथा । तद् यस्माज् जातं स एव विष्णुः । उ इति संबोधने । प्रावीविशत् प्रकर्षेणालुप्त-शक्तिर् एवान्तर्यामितया विवेश । तस्मिन् विष्णुनाधिष्ठिते पद्मे विधाता ब्रह्माभूत् । कथं भूतः ? स्वयम् एव वेद-मयो, न त्व् अध्ययनेन प्राप्त-वेदः । कोऽसौ ? अदृष्ट-पितृत्वेन यं स्वयम्-भुवं वदन्ति सः । प्राक्-कल्पान्ते नारायणेन सह निद्रयैकी-भूत आसीत् तस्मिंश् च प्रबुद्धे, तत एव पाद्मे कल्पे पद्म-द्वारेणाभिव्यक्तिं प्राप्त इत्य् अर्थः ॥१५॥
word_for_word: tal-lokātmakaṃ padmaṃ sarvān guṇān jīva-bhogyān arthān avabhāsayatīti tathā
The lotus is called the form of the worlds because it illumines all the objects
tad yasmāj jātaṃ sa eva viṣṇuḥ
qualities and experiences available to living beings. The one from whom it was born was Viṣṇu. O Lord
u iti saṃbodhane
He entered it fully
prāvīviśat prakarṣeṇālupta-śaktir evāntaryāmitayā viveśa
without any loss of power
tasmin viṣṇunādhiṣṭhite padme vidhātā brahmābhūt
as its indwelling controller. In that lotus presided over by Viṣṇu
kathaṃ bhūtaḥ ? svayam eva veda-mayo
Brahmā became the creator
na tv adhyayanena prāpta-vedaḥ
himself made of the Veda and endowed with the power to create.
ko’sau ? adṛṣṭa-pitṛtvena yaṃ svayam-bhuvaṃ vadanti saḥ
himself made of the Veda and endowed with the power to create.
prāk-kalpānte nārāyaṇena saha nidrayaikī-bhūta āsīt tasmiṃś ca prabuddhe

tata eva pādme kalpe padma-dvāreṇābhivyaktiṃ prāpta ity arthaḥ

entries.literal_english: The lotus is called the form of the worlds because it illumines all the objects, qualities and experiences available to living beings. The one from whom it was born was Viṣṇu. O Lord, He entered it fully, without any loss of power, as its indwelling controller. In that lotus presided over by Viṣṇu, Brahmā became the creator, himself made of the Veda and endowed with the power to create.

entries.sanskrit: स च तस्मिन् कल्पे चतुर्-मुखोऽभूद् इत्य् आह---तस्याम् इति । परिक्रमंस् तत्र-स्थ एव ग्रीवां चालयन् लोक-निरीक्षणार्थं विवृत्ते विचलिते नेत्रे यस्य ॥१६॥
word_for_word: sa ca tasmin kalpe catur-mukho’bhūd ity āha
He became four-faced in that kalpa. Remaining there
tasyām iti
he moved around and turned his neck in order to inspect the worlds
parikramaṃs tatra-stha eva grīvāṃ cālayan loka-nirīkṣaṇārthaṃ vivṛtte vicalite netre yasya
his eyes turned in different directions.

entries.sanskrit: तस्य च श्री-नारायणोपासनयैवाविर्भूत-ज्ञान-क्रिया-शक्तेर् लोक-कर्तृत्वं न स्वत इति वक्तुं प्रथमं तस्य विमोहम् आह---तस्मात् सलिलाद् विरूढम् उद्गतं कञ्जम् उपाश्रियोऽपि साकल्येन तत् कञ्जं लोक-तत्त्वं चात्मानं च साक्षान् न ज्ञातवान् । उ इति विस्मये। कथं-भूतात् ? युगान्त-श्वसनः प्रलय-वायुस् तेनावघूर्णं तत्र तत्र प्रकम्पितं यस्मात् सर्वत ऊर्मि-चक्रं यस्मिन् ॥१७॥
word_for_word: tasya ca śrī-nārāyaṇopāsanayaivāvirbhūta-jñāna-kriyā-śakter loka-kartṛtvaṃ na svata iti vaktuṃ prathamaṃ tasya vimoham āha
Maitreya first describes Brahmā’s bewilderment to show that Brahmā’s power to create the worlds arose only through worship of Śrī Nārāyaṇa
tasmāt salilād virūḍham udgataṃ kañjam upāśriyo’pi sākalyena tat kañjaṃ loka-tattvaṃ cātmānaṃ ca sākṣān na jñātavān
not independently. Although he had taken shelter of the lotus grown from the water
u iti vismaye
he could not fully know the lotus
kathaṃ-bhūtāt ? yugānta-śvasanaḥ pralaya-vāyus tenāvaghūrṇaṃ tatra tatra prakampitaṃ yasmāt sarvata ūrmi-cakraṃ yasmin
the principles of the worlds
or himself. The expressions of wonder and the description of the vast waters indicate the difficulty of the search.
entries.literal_english: Maitreya first describes Brahmā’s bewilderment to show that Brahmā’s power to create the worlds arose only through worship of Śrī Nārāyaṇa, not independently. Although he had taken shelter of the lotus grown from the water, he could not fully know the lotus, the principles of the worlds, or himself. The expressions of wonder and the description of the vast waters indicate the difficulty of the search.

entries.sanskrit: अविदुषस् तस्य वितर्कम् आह---योऽसाव् अहम् अब्ज-पृष्ठे एष कः ? अनन्यद् एकम् एवैतद् अब्जं कुतो वा जातं ? यत्रैतद् अधिष्ठितं तेनाधस्तात् सता वर्तमानेन नु निश्चितं भाव्यम् । स इत्थम् उद्वीक्ष्येत्य् उत्तरेणान्वयः । तथा च श्रुतिः---सोऽपश्यत् पुष्कर-पर्णे तिष्ठन् सोऽमन्यत अस्ति चैतद् यस्मिन्न् इदम् अधितिष्ठति इति ॥१८॥
word_for_word: aviduṣas tasya vitarkam āha
The thought of the ignorant Brahmā is described
yo’sāv aham abja-pṛṣṭhe eṣa kaḥ ? ananyad ekam evaitad abjaṃ kuto vā jātaṃ ? yatraitad adhiṣṭhitaṃ tenādhastāt satā vartamānena nu niścitaṃ bhāvyam

entries.sanskrit: तस्य च बहिर्-मुख-प्रवृत्त्या महतापि कालेन तद् अप्राप्तिम् आह---स इति द्वाभ्याम् । तस्याब्जसय यन् नालं तस्य नाडीभिर् अन्तश् छिद्रैः । तस्य स्वर-नालस्य पद्मस्य यन् नालं तस्य नाभिम् अधिष्ठानं विचिन्वन्न् अर्वाग्-गतोऽपि तत् तदा नाविन्दत ॥१९॥
word_for_word: tasya ca bahir-mukha-pravṛttyā mahatāpi kālena tad aprāptim āha
Because he turned outward
sa iti dvābhyām

tasyābjasaya yan nālaṃ tasya nāḍībhir antaś chidraiḥ
looking for its navel and foundation
tasya svara-nālasya padmasya yan nālaṃ tasya nābhim adhiṣṭhānaṃ vicinvann arvāg-gato’pi tat tadā nāvindata
but although he went downward he did not discover it then.

entries.literal_english: Because he turned outward, even after a very long time he did not find the source. He searched through the inner channels and openings of the lotus stalk, looking for its navel and foundation, but although he went downward he did not discover it then.

entries.sanskrit: हे विदुर, आत्म-सर्गं स्व-कारणम् । त्रिणेमिः कालः । अजस्य विष्णोर् हेतिः सुदर्शन-रूपं शस्त्रम् । देह-भाजां नराणां भयम् उत्पादयन्न् इति संवत्सर-शतम् इत्य् उक्तं भवति ॥२०॥
word_for_word: he vidura
O Vidura
ātma-sargaṃ sva-kāraṇam
“self-creation” means the Lord’s own causal creation. The three-spoked wheel is time. The weapon of unborn Viṣṇu is Sudarśana
triṇemiḥ kālaḥ
which produces fear in embodied beings
ajasya viṣṇor hetiḥ sudarśana-rūpaṃ śastram
“a hundred years” therefore means a period of a hundred divine years.
deha-bhājāṃ narāṇāṃ bhayam utpādayann iti saṃvatsara-śatam ity uktaṃ bhavati

entries.sanskrit: अन्तर्-मुखतया तु भगवन्तं दृष्टवान् इत्य् आह द्वाभ्याम् । ततोऽन्वेषणान् निवृत्तः । न प्रतिलब्धः कामो मनो-रथो येन । स्व-धिष्ण्यं पद्मम् । जितेन श्वासेन निवृत्तं संयतं चित्तं यस्य, अत एवारूढ आश्रितः समाधि-योगो येन तथा-भूतः सन् न्यषीदद् उपविवेश ॥२१॥
word_for_word: antar-mukhatayā tu bhagavantaṃ dṛṣṭavān ity āha dvābhyām
When he turned inward
tato’nveṣaṇān nivṛttaḥ
he saw Bhagavān
na pratilabdhaḥ kāmo mano-ratho yena
as the next two verses explain. He stopped searching because the desired object had not been found. He returned to his own lotus-seat

entries.sanskrit: महा-चन्दन-वृक्ष-रूपकेण निरूपयितुं तं विशिनष्टि । परार्ध्यानि श्रेष्ठानि केयूराण्य् अङ्गदानि मणि-प्रवेकाश् च मण्य्-उत्तमास् तैः पर्यस्ता व्याप्ता दोर्-दण्डा एव सहस्रम् अनन्ताः शाखा यस्य । चन्दन-वृक्षोऽपि केयूरादि-तुल्यैः फल-पुष्पादिभिर् व्याप्त-शाखो भवति । अव्यक्तं प्रधानं मूलम् अधो-भागो यस्य । यद् वा, अव्यक्तं ब्रह्म मूलं यस्य, ब्रह्माभिव्यक्ति-रूपत्वात् । वृक्षस्यापि मूलं न व्यक्तम् । भूवनात्मकम् अङ्घ्रिपेन्द्रम् । अहीन्द्रस्यानन्तस्य भोगैः फणैर् देहावयवैर् वाधिवीताः संवेष्टिताः स्पृष्टा वल्शाः स्कन्धा यस्य,वनस्पते शत-वल्शो विरोह \[ऋग्।वे। ३.८.४\] इति श्रुतेः । सोऽपि सर्पैर् वेष्टितो भवति ॥२९॥

entries.literal_english: He is described through the image of a great sandalwood tree. His arms were like countless branches covered with excellent armlets, bracelets and the finest jewels. entries.sanskrit: प्रेक्षां क्षिपन्तम् इत्य् अत्रैव पर्वत-रूपकेण निरूपितम् अपि विशेषणान्तरैः पुनर् निरूपयति । भगवान् एव मही-ध्रस्तम् । चराचराणाम् ओकः स्थानम् । सोऽपि तथा । अहीन्द्रस्य बन्धुम् । सोऽप्य् अहीन्द्राणां बन्धुः । सलिलेनोपगूढम् आवृतम् । पर्वतोऽपि मैनाकादिस् तथा । किरीट-साहस्रम् एव हिरण्य-शृङ्गाणि यस्य । सोऽपि मेर्वादिस् तथा । यथा पर्वतस्य गर्भे क्वचिद् रत्नम् आविर्भवति तथा आविर्भवत् स्पष्टं दृश्यमानं कौस्तुभ-रत्नं गर्भे मूर्ति-मध्ये यस्य तम् ॥३०॥

entries.sanskrit: किं च, वन-मालया निवीतं कण्ठ-लम्बिन्या व्याप्तम् । आम्नाया वेदा एव मधु-व्रताः, तैः श्रीर् यस्यास् तया हरिम् इति पर्वतादि-रूपम् अपश्यत्, हरिर् असाव् इति ज्ञातवान् इत्य् अर्थः । सूर्यादिभिर् अगमम् अगम्यम् । स्व-व्यापारैर् आकलयितुम् अशक्यम् इत्य् अर्थः । किं च, त्रिष्व् अपि लोकेषु धाम स्फूर्तिर् येषां तैः । रक्षणार्थं परिक्रमद्भिः परितो धावद्भिः प्राधनिकैः प्रधनं सङ्ग्रामस् तत्-प्रयोजनैः सुदर्शनादिभिर् हेतु-भूतैर् दुरासदं दुष्प्रापम् ॥३१॥

entries.literal_english: After seeing Hari, Brahmā saw the scene of the creation of the worlds: the lotus in the Lord’s navel, His breathing, the wind of dissolution, and the ether.

entries.sanskrit: कर्म-बीजं लोक-सृष्टेः कारणम् । रजसा उपरक्तो रजो-गुण-युक्तः । अतः प्रजाः स्रष्टुम् इच्छन्न् इयद् एव नाभि-सरोजादि-पञ्चकम् एव । विसर्गेऽप्य् अभिमुख-उदत्त-चित्तः अव्यक्त-वर्त्मनि भगवति निवेशित-चित्तः ॥३३॥
word_for_word: karma-bījaṃ loka-sṛṣṭeḥ kāraṇam
The seed of karma is the cause of the creation of the worlds. Brahmā
rajasā uparakto rajo-guṇa-yuktaḥ
colored by rajas and joined to the rajasic quality
ataḥ prajāḥ sraṣṭum icchann iyad eva nābhi-sarojādi-pañcakam eva
desired to create the beings. His mind was directed to the fivefold object beginning with the lotus of the navel
visarge’py abhimukha-udatta-cittaḥ avyakta-vartmani bhagavati niveśita-cittaḥ
and even during creation his attention was fixed on Bhagavān
the unmanifest source.
entries.literal_english: The seed of karma is the cause of the creation of the worlds. Brahmā, colored by rajas and joined to the rajasic quality, desired to create the beings. His mind was directed to the fivefold object beginning with the lotus of the navel, and even during creation his attention was fixed on Bhagavān, the unmanifest source.
